item.mechanism: High volumetric energy input and slow scan speeds promote the dissolution of high-melting particles (specifically Tungsten) during in-situ alloy formation by increasing re-melting, interaction time, and favorable powder movement.
item.system: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 refractory metal high entropy alloy produced from elemental powder mixtures
item.operating_conditions: PBF-LB/M processing; Parameter set B: 100 mm/s scan speed, 889 J/mm³ volumetric energy density; Parameter set A: 800 mm/s scan speed, 125 J/mm³ volumetric energy density
item.supporting_observation: Parameter set PBF-LB/M B, with lower scan speed and higher volumetric energy density, resulted in fewer undissolved Tungsten particles compared to parameter set A, which contained undissolved W particles.
item.scope_limits: Does not hold for parameter sets with high scan speeds and low volumetric energy input (e.g., PBF-LB/M A) where undissolved particles persist; specific to high-melting elements like W in mixtures with large melting point differences.
item.alternatives_considered: Pre-alloyed powder atomization (not used here due to cost); other parameter combinations not tested in this specific comparison.
quotes: According to [ [32] ] a high volumetric energy input, slow scan speeds, and accordingly reduced laser power support the dissolution of high melting elements at in-situ alloy formation by PBF-LB/M.

Parameter set PBF-LB/M B comprises a considerably lower scan speed (100 mm/s vs. 800 mm/s) but, despite the lower laser power, a higher volumetric energy density (889 J/mm 3 vs. 125 J/mm 3 ) than parameter set PBF-LB/M A.
This facilitates the dissolution of the high melting W particles, thus leading to less undissolved particles as shown in Figure 2 .

item.mechanism: Cracking in the solidified material is caused by internal stresses induced by the PBF-LB/M process combined with the alloy's insufficient ductility and brittle grain boundaries at lower temperatures.
item.system: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 refractory metal high entropy alloy
item.operating_conditions: PBF-LB/M processing at room temperature build platform; Parameter sets A and B; presence of O and N impurities at grain boundaries
item.supporting_observation: Cracks are mostly perpendicular to the build direction and are attributed to internal stress and low ductility rather than hot cracking; wider cracks occur with higher energy density and smaller hatch distance.
item.scope_limits: Hot cracking is excluded as the main cause; mechanism assumes room temperature brittleness; does not hold if high temperature build-platform heating or high purity powder is used.
item.alternatives_considered: Hot cracking (related to solidification of the alloy) was considered but excluded based on crack structure.
quotes: Instead, cracking of the already solidified material due to internal stress induced by the PBF-LB/M process and an insufficient ductility of the material at lower temperatures is assumed to be the cause for the cracks.
The brittle grain boundaries in combination with the internal stress induced during PBF-LB/M consequently lead to cracking of the samples during processing.

The different crack patterns in dependence of the parameter set PBF-LB/M A and PBF-LB/M B with wider cracks in the PBF-LB/M B samples are a result of the smaller hatch distance (45 µm vs. 120 µm) and the higher volumetric energy density applied (889 J/mm 3 vs. 125 J/mm 3 ) compared to parameter set PBF-LB/M A.

item.mechanism: High cooling rates inherent to PBF-LB/M (approx. 10^6 K/s) mitigate elemental segregation during solidification and result in significantly finer grain sizes compared to conventional casting methods.
item.system: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 refractory metal high entropy alloy
item.operating_conditions: PBF-LB/M processing with cooling rates in the range of 10^6 K/s
item.supporting_observation: Average grain size of 16.3 µm was observed, which is more than four times smaller than the 80 µm reported for vacuum arc molten samples; homogeneity of element distribution is better than in vacuum arc melted samples.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the high cooling rates of PBF-LB/M; does not apply to slow cooling methods like vacuum arc melting or casting without homogenization.
item.alternatives_considered: Vacuum arc melting and casting with long homogenization heat treatments (>>1 day) were considered as conventional methods but are laborious.
quotes: Furthermore, small meltpool dimensions of a few hundred µm and high cooling rates in the range of 10 6 K/s [ [29] ] during PBF-LB/M are presumed to mitigate segregation of elements during solidification which is of importance with regard to refractory metal high entropy alloys [ [18] ].
The average grain size determined by the linear intercept method is 16.3 µm. This is more than a factor of four smaller than the 80 µm reported by Senkov et al. for vacuum arc molten samples.
The smaller grain size can be attributed to the high cooling rates in the range of 10 6 K/s during the PBF-LB/M process [ [50] ].

item.mechanism: Solidification mode (dendritic vs. cellular) and resulting microstructure size are determined by the ratio of growth rate (R) and temperature gradient (G) in the liquid melt pool, which are functions of laser scan speed and hatch distance.
item.system: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 refractory metal high entropy alloy
item.operating_conditions: PBF-LB/M processing; Parameter set A (high scan speed, large melt pool) vs. Parameter set B (low scan speed, small melt pool)
item.supporting_observation: Parameter set A (higher R, lower G) produced a coarser dendritic structure, while Parameter set B (lower R, higher G) produced an almost cellular structure.
item.scope_limits: Dependent on the specific relationship between scan speed, hatch distance, and melt pool dimensions; assumes evaporation temperature defines upper melt pool limit.
item.alternatives_considered: Other solidification modes not observed in this specific parameter comparison.
quotes: According to the literature [ [52] , [53] ] the solidification mode and also the structure size is determined by R and G.

While higher growth rates R and lower temperature gradients G in the liquid favor a columnar dendritic solidification, lower growth rates R and higher temperature gradients in the liquid G favor cellular solidification.

Parameter set PBF-LB/M A features a larger structure size and more distinct secondary dendrites, while the material processed with parameter set PBF-LB/M B solidifies in an almost cellular structure with only a few secondary dendrites.

item.mechanism: Segregation of alloying elements occurs during solidification where low-melting elements (Vanadium) concentrate in interdendritic areas and high-melting elements (Tungsten, Tantalum) concentrate in intradendritic areas.
item.system: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 refractory metal high entropy alloy
item.operating_conditions: Solidification during PBF-LB/M; analyzed via EDS and TEM-EDS
item.supporting_observation: EDS and TEM-EDS show Vanadium concentrated in interdendritic areas, while W and Ta are predominantly located in intradendritic areas; Nb and Mo are almost equally distributed.
item.scope_limits: Observed in both parameter sets A and B; homogeneity is better than in vacuum arc melted samples but segregation still exists.
item.alternatives_considered: Complete homogeneity without segregation (not achieved); segregation patterns similar to vacuum arc melted samples.
quotes: As shown in Figure 7 Vanadium, which is the lowest melting element [ [54] ] in the WMoTaNbV alloy, is concentrated in the interdendritic areas, while the intradendritic areas lack Vanadium.
Nb and Mo are almost equally distributed between inter- and intradendritic regions, while Ta and especially W are predominantly located in the intradendritic areas.

Mo and Nb are almost equally distributed between interdendritic and intradendritic areas, while there is a considerable W and a weak Ta surplus in the intradendritic regions. V is predominantly concentrated in the interdendritic areas of the material.

item.mechanism: Microhardness is influenced by the solidification mode and microstructure size; finer cellular structures (from lower growth rates/higher gradients) result in higher hardness than coarser dendritic structures.
item.system: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 refractory metal high entropy alloy
item.operating_conditions: PBF-LB/M processing; Parameter set A (dendritic) vs. Parameter set B (cellular)
item.supporting_observation: Microhardness of PBF-LB/M A (coarser) was 561 ± 17 HV0.1, while PBF-LB/M B (cellular) was 614 ± 21 HV0.1.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the microstructural differences induced by the two parameter sets; does not account for other strengthening mechanisms like precipitation.
item.alternatives_considered: Other factors affecting hardness not isolated in this study.
quotes: These different solidification modes also affect the material properties.
The microhardness of the PBF-LB/M A sample with the coarser structure is 561 ± 17 HV0.1 (n = 9) while the microhardness of the PBF-LB/M B sample is 614 ± 21 HV0.1 (n = 9).
This demonstrates that the alloy WMoTaNbV is sensitive to the processing conditions which are determined by the PBF-LB/M parameters.

item.mechanism: Selective evaporation of lower boiling point elements (specifically Vanadium) occurs during PBF-LB/M, necessitating a pre-compensation of the initial powder mixture to achieve the target composition.
item.system: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 refractory metal high entropy alloy
item.operating_conditions: PBF-LB/M processing with laser power up to 1 kW; Argon shielding gas
item.supporting_observation: The amount of Vanadium in the initial powder mixture was increased by a factor of 1.5 compared to other elements to pre-compensate for expected evaporation.
item.scope_limits: Specific to elements with low boiling points relative to the process temperature; Vanadium has the lowest boiling point in the system.
item.alternatives_considered: Using pre-alloyed powder to avoid evaporation issues (not used here).
quotes: Since selective evaporation of lower boiling alloying elements is a common phenomenon in PBF-LB/M [ [41] ], the amount of Vanadium, which has the lowest boiling point in the WMoNbTaV system [ [26] ], in the initial powder mixture was increased by a factor of 1.5 compared to the other alloying elements to pre-compensate the expected evaporation of V during PBF-LB/M.

item.mechanism: The formation of a single bcc-phase is achievable via in-situ alloy formation in PBF-LB/M, confirming the feasibility of producing refractory metal high entropy alloys without pre-alloyed powder.
item.system: W20Mo20Ta20Nb20V20 refractory metal high entropy alloy
item.operating_conditions: PBF-LB/M processing; analyzed by EBSD and TEM
item.supporting_observation: EBSD and TEM measurements confirm the presence of a single bcc-phase in samples produced from elemental powder mixtures.
item.scope_limits: Dependent on selecting favorable process parameter combinations to ensure complete fusion; does not hold if significant undissolved particles or segregation prevent single-phase formation.
item.alternatives_considered: Formation of multiple phases or intermetallic compounds (not observed in successful samples).
quotes: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) measurements confirm the presence of a single bcc-phase.
The sample consists entirely of a single bcc high entropy phase, which is in agreement with the results of Senkov et al. for vacuum arc molten WMoTaNbV [ [18] , [19] ].
This confirms the feasibility of producing refractory metal high entropy alloys by PBF-LB/M and in-situ alloy formation.
